result.markdown: --- title: "Ensemble prediction with multiple models" format: html --- ### Configurations to run this chapter{-} :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # load package "tibble" library(tibble) # load packages "sits" and "sitsdata" library(sits) library(sitsdata) # set tempdir if it does not exist tempdir_r <- "~/sitsbook/tempdir/R/cl_ensembleprediction" dir.create(tempdir_r, showWarnings = FALSE) ``` ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} # load "pysits" library from pysits import * from pathlib import Path # set tempdir if it does not exist tempdir_py = Path.home() / "sitsbook/tempdir/Python/cl_ensembleprediction" tempdir_py.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: ## Introduction to ensemble prediction Ensemble prediction is a powerful technique for combining predictions from multiple models to produce more accurate and robust predictions. Errors of individual models cancel out or are reduced when combined with the predictions of other models. As a result, ensemble predictions can lead to better overall accuracy and reduce the risk of overfitting. This can be especially useful when working with complex or uncertain data. By combining the predictions of multiple models, users can identify which features or factors are most important for making accurate predictions. When using ensemble methods, choosing diverse models with different sources of error is essential to ensure that the ensemble predictions are more precise and robust. The `sits` package provides `sits_combine_predictions()` to estimate ensemble predictions using probability cubes produced by `sits_classify()` and optionally post-processed with `sits_smooth()`. There are two ways to make ensemble predictions from multiple models: * *Averaging*: In this approach, the predictions of each model are averaged to produce the final prediction. This method works well when the models have similar accuracy and errors. * *Uncertainty*: Predictions from different models are compared in terms of their uncertainties on a pixel-by-pixel basis; predictions with lower uncertainty are chosen as being more likely to be valid. In what follows, we will use the same sample dataset and data cube used in Chapter [Image classification in data cubes](https://e-sensing.github.io/sitsbook/cl_rasterclassification.html) to illustrate how to produce an ensemble prediction. The dataset `samples_deforestation_rondonia` consists of 6,007 samples collected from Sentinel-2 images covering the state of Rondonia. Each time series contains values from all Sentinel-2/2A spectral bands for year 2022 in 16-day intervals. The data cube is a subset of the Sentinel-2 tile "20LMR" which contains all spectral bands, plus spectral indices "NVDI", "EVI" and "NBR" for the year 2022. ## Recovering the data cube The first step is to recover the data cube which is available in the `sitsdata` package, and to select only the spectral bands. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-cube-20LMR_6e88479625341df539f5d8b3827a7cd2'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Files are available in a local directory data_dir <- system.file("extdata/Rondonia-20LMR/", package = "sitsdata") # Read data cube ro_cube_20LMR <- sits_cube( source = "MPC", collection = "SENTINEL-2-L2A", data_dir = data_dir ) # reduce the number of bands ro_cube_20LMR <- sits_select( data = ro_cube_20LMR, bands = c( "B02", "B03", "B04", "B05", "B06", "B07", "B08", "B11", "B12", "B8A" ) ) # plot one time step of the cube plot( ro_cube_20LMR, blue = "B02", green = "B8A", red = "B11", date = "2022-08-17" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} !["Subset of Sentinel-2 tile 20LMR." ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-cube-20LMR-1.png){#fig-cube-20LMR fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} # Files are available in a local directory data_dir = r_package_dir("extdata/Rondonia-20LMR/", package = "sitsdata") # Read data cube ro_cube_20LMR = sits_cube( source = "MPC", collection = "SENTINEL-2-L2A", data_dir = data_dir ) # reduce the number of bands ro_cube_20LMR = sits_select( data = ro_cube_20LMR, bands = ( "B02", "B03", "B04", "B05", "B06", "B07", "B08", "B11", "B12", "B8A" ) ) # plot one time step of the cube plot( ro_cube_20LMR, blue = "B02", green = "B8A", red = "B11", date = "2022-08-17" ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-fig-cube-20LMR_def1f5934d1fb94d7baa8830c4823bd1'} ::: {.cell-output-display} !["Subset of Sentinel-2 tile 20LMR." ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/py-fig-cube-20LMR-1.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: ## Classification using Random Forest We will train three models: Random Forest (RF), Light Temporal Attention Encoder (LTAE), and Temporal Convolution Neural Networks (TempCNN), classify the cube with them, and then combine their results. The example uses all spectral bands. We first run the RF classification. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-ensemble-rfor-probs_e0acc04ce698611fdc79d3babdcc0a94'} ```{.r .cell-code} # train a Random Forest model rfor_model <- sits_train(samples_deforestation_rondonia, sits_rfor()) # classify the data cube ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs <- sits_classify( ro_cube_20LMR, rfor_model, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) # plot the probabilities for class Forest plot(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs, labels = "Forest") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Plot of probabilities for class Forest produced by Random Forest algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-ensemble-rfor-probs-1.png){#fig-ensemble-rfor-probs fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} # load data samples_deforestation_rondonia = load_samples( name = "samples_deforestation_rondonia", package = "sitsdata" ) # train a Random Forest model rfor_model = sits_train(samples_deforestation_rondonia, sits_rfor()) # classify the data cube ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs = sits_classify( ro_cube_20LMR, rfor_model, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) # plot the probabilities for class Forest plot(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs, labels = "Forest") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-fig-ensemble-rfor-probs_b04be96e012892dda52d138991134947'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Plot of probabilities for class Forest produced by Random Forest algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/py-fig-ensemble-rfor-probs-1.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell result='true' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/unnamed-chunk-6_1002dc4f4aadc095c44074f6806f22d9'} ```{.r .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_variance <- sits_variance( ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs, window_size = 9, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) summary(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_variance) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil Clear_Cut_Burned_Area Clear_Cut_Vegetation Forest 75% 4.05 5.05 0.330 0.7325 80% 4.82 5.44 0.400 1.0300 85% 5.37 5.71 0.510 1.5300 90% 5.80 6.01 0.771 3.2410 95% 6.40 6.78 3.600 6.0900 100% 17.27 16.68 13.090 24.8300 Mountainside_Forest Riparian_Forest Seasonally_Flooded Water Wetland 75% 4.39 0.5700 0.3100 0.0200 4.91 80% 5.01 0.7100 0.3700 0.2500 5.35 85% 5.48 1.0400 0.4900 0.5900 5.66 90% 5.83 2.0420 0.7210 1.8400 5.96 95% 6.29 4.8005 1.4205 6.6645 6.48 100% 10.47 43.1800 20.3600 50.1700 30.29 ``` ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_variance = sits_variance( ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs, window_size = 9, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) summary(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_variance) ``` ::: ::: {.cell result='true' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/unnamed-chunk-8_e91b6a7bd460d0a3d5258e58770ea9c8'} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil Clear_Cut_Burned_Area Clear_Cut_Vegetation Forest 75% 4.000 4.960 0.3300 0.7400 80% 4.842 5.380 0.4000 1.0300 85% 5.440 5.680 0.5100 1.5500 90% 5.800 6.001 0.7800 3.2300 95% 6.460 6.730 3.4905 6.2705 100% 19.300 15.530 13.2900 25.8800 Mountainside_Forest Riparian_Forest Seasonally_Flooded Water Wetland 75% 4.550 0.600 0.3200 0.0400 4.91 80% 5.132 0.770 0.4000 0.5300 5.35 85% 5.550 1.140 0.5200 0.8800 5.65 90% 5.870 2.261 0.7510 2.1600 5.95 95% 6.320 5.040 1.3905 7.9605 6.45 100% 10.580 38.550 16.8200 52.3200 17.98 ``` ::: ::: ::: Based on the variance values, we apply the smoothness hyperparameter according to the recommendations proposed before. We choose values of $\sigma^2_{k}$ that reflect our prior expectation of the spatial patterns of each class. For classes `Clear_Cut_Vegetation` and `Clear_Cut_Burned_Area`, to produce denser spatial clusters and remove "salt-and-pepper" outliers, we take $\sigma^2_{k}$ values in 95%-100% range. In the case of the most frequent classes `Forest` and `Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil` we want to preserve their original spatial shapes as much as possible; the same logic applies to less frequent classes `Water` and `Wetland`. For this reason, we set $\sigma^2_{k}$ values in the 75%-80% range for these classes. The class spatial patterns correspond to our prior expectations. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-ensemble-rfor-class_9ec7df538973f7d2b7ae2890312ffa4f'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Smoothen the probability cube ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_bayes <- sits_smooth( ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs, output_dir = tempdir_r, smoothness = c( "Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil" = 5.25, "Clear_Cut_Burned_Area" = 15.0, "Clear_Cut_Vegetation" = 12.0, "Forest" = 1.8, "Mountainside_Forest" = 6.5, "Riparian_Forest" = 6.0, "Seasonally_Flooded" = 3.5, "Water" = 1.5, "Wetland" = 5.5), multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) # Classify the cube ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_class <- sits_label_classification( ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_bayes, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) plot(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_class, legend_text_size = 0.7, legend_position = "outside") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Classified map produced by Random Forest algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-ensemble-rfor-class-1.png){#fig-ensemble-rfor-class fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_bayes = sits_smooth( ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_probs, output_dir = tempdir_py, smoothness = dict( Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil = 5.25, Clear_Cut_Burned_Area = 15.0, Clear_Cut_Vegetation = 12.0, Forest = 1.8, Mountainside_Forest = 6.5, Riparian_Forest = 6.0, Seasonally_Flooded = 3.5, Water = 1.5, Wetland = 5.5), multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_class = sits_label_classification( ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_bayes, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "rfor" ) plot(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_class, legend_text_size = 0.7, legend_position = "outside") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-fig-ensemble-rfor-class_5e2a80e420ba814d6ebee6e9acc5b921'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Plot of probabilities for class Forest produced by Random Forest algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/py-fig-ensemble-rfor-class-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ## Classification using Temporal Convolution Neural Networks (TempCNN) The next step is to classify the same area using a tempCNN algorithm, as shown below. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-ensemble-tcnn-probs_1c49b1febaa8a1d3b3b639507c26df2a'} ```{.r .cell-code} # train a tempcnn model tcnn_model <- sits_train(samples_deforestation_rondonia, sits_tempcnn()) # classify the data cube ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs <- sits_classify( ro_cube_20LMR, tcnn_model, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 2, memsize = 8, gpu_memory = 8, version = "tcnn" ) # plot the probabilities for class Forest plot(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs, labels = "Forest") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Plot of probabilities for class Forest produced by TempCNN algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-ensemble-tcnn-probs-1.png){#fig-ensemble-tcnn-probs fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} # train a tempcnn model tcnn_model = sits_train(samples_deforestation_rondonia, sits_tempcnn()) # classify the data cube ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs = sits_classify( ro_cube_20LMR, tcnn_model, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 2, memsize = 8, gpu_memory = 8, version = "tcnn" ) # plot the probabilities for class Forest plot(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs, labels = "Forest") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-fig-ensemble-tcnn-probs_3cdaecfae41fda50faf29f0938c58456'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Plot of probabilities for class Forest produced by TempCNN algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/py-fig-ensemble-tcnn-probs-1.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: Now we calculate the variance of the probability cube. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/ensemble-tcnn-variance_82ad96ae73fa8634e182fb9ec4e64c8d'} ```{.r .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_variance <- sits_variance( ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs, window_size = 9, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "tcnn" ) summary(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_variance) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil Clear_Cut_Burned_Area Clear_Cut_Vegetation Forest 75% 1.01 1.0700 1.56 2.0700 80% 1.28 1.3400 1.84 2.5600 85% 1.78 1.7200 2.23 3.3100 90% 2.96 2.3810 2.93 4.7000 95% 6.38 3.6705 4.64 8.1205 100% 30.83 35.7700 25.06 39.2800 Mountainside_Forest Riparian_Forest Seasonally_Flooded Water Wetland 75% 1.16 2.2500 2.0600 0.650 1.56 80% 1.39 2.7300 2.5100 0.820 1.88 85% 1.69 3.4100 3.2300 1.060 2.33 90% 2.13 4.5210 4.5500 1.570 3.03 95% 2.86 7.0205 7.7205 9.111 4.45 100% 11.99 46.5300 43.9900 54.150 35.89 ``` ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_variance = sits_variance( ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs, window_size = 9, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "tcnn" ) summary(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_variance) ``` ::: ::: {.cell hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-ensemble-tcnn-variance_bf47ca65527900f944eef4f88c019f7a'} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil Clear_Cut_Burned_Area Clear_Cut_Vegetation Forest 75% 0.9700 1.07 1.5300 1.99 80% 1.2600 1.32 1.8300 2.50 85% 1.7800 1.72 2.2100 3.28 90% 3.0010 2.33 2.8610 4.68 95% 5.9305 3.65 4.5205 8.08 100% 29.3400 22.88 32.1500 41.37 Mountainside_Forest Riparian_Forest Seasonally_Flooded Water Wetland 75% 1.1625 2.2000 2.0700 0.6400 1.58 80% 1.4000 2.6400 2.5300 0.7900 1.91 85% 1.7000 3.3400 3.2200 1.0400 2.38 90% 2.1500 4.4200 4.5100 1.5300 3.07 95% 2.8700 6.8905 7.4605 8.8905 4.50 100% 9.6500 52.5200 38.6000 57.5100 33.87 ``` ::: ::: ::: Based on the variance results, we perform a spatial smoothing and classify the data cube. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-ensemble-tcnn-class_4dd613fe796347d9aab0701e061e1e61'} ```{.r .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_bayes <- sits_smooth( ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs, output_dir = tempdir_r, window_size = 11, smoothness = c( "Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil" = 1.5, "Clear_Cut_Burned_Area" = 20.0, "Clear_Cut_Vegetation" = 25.0, "Forest" = 4.0, "Mountainside_Forest" = 3.0, "Riparian_Forest" = 40.0, "Seasonally_Flooded" = 30.0, "Water" = 1.0, "Wetland" = 2.0), multicores = 2, memsize = 6, version = "tcnn" ) ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_class <- sits_label_classification( ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_bayes, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 2, memsize = 6, version = "tcnn" ) plot(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_class, legend_text_size = 0.7, legend_position = "outside") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Classified map produced by TempCNN algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-ensemble-tcnn-class-1.png){#fig-ensemble-tcnn-class fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_bayes = sits_smooth( ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs, output_dir = tempdir_py, window_size = 11, smoothness = dict( Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil = 1.5, Clear_Cut_Burned_Area = 20.0, Clear_Cut_Vegetation = 25.0, Forest = 4.0, Mountainside_Forest = 3.0, Riparian_Forest = 40.0, Seasonally_Flooded = 30.0, Water = 1.0, Wetland = 2.0), multicores = 2, memsize = 6, version = "tcnn" ) ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_class = sits_label_classification( ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_bayes, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 2, memsize = 6, version = "tcnn" ) plot(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_class, legend_text_size = 0.7, legend_position = "outside") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-fig-ensemble-tcnn-class_f0af9b1519c7e8a181968c062d043116'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Classified map produced by TempCNN algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/py-fig-ensemble-tcnn-class-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ## Classification using Lightweight Temporal Attention Encoder (LTAE) The third model is the Light Temporal Attention Encoder (LTAE), which has been discussed in the Machine Learning chapter. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-ensemble-ltae-probs_96c3b87b131b4f6e3fe193262e6a6d64'} ```{.r .cell-code} # train a tempcnn model ltae_model <- sits_train(samples_deforestation_rondonia, sits_lighttae()) # classify the data cube ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_probs <- sits_classify( ro_cube_20LMR, ltae_model, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 2, memsize = 6, gpu_memory = 2, version = "ltae" ) # plot the probabilities for class Forest plot(ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_probs, labels = "Forest") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Plot of probabilities for class Forest produced by LTAE algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-ensemble-ltae-probs-1.png){#fig-ensemble-ltae-probs fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} # train a tempcnn model ltae_model = sits_train(samples_deforestation_rondonia, sits_lighttae()) # classify the data cube ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_probs = sits_classify( ro_cube_20LMR, ltae_model, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 2, memsize = 8, gpu_memory = 8, version = "ltae" ) # plot the probabilities for class Forest plot(ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_probs, labels = "Forest") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-fig-ensemble-ltae-probs_1c84f7bd67bbda77906e525590a113e8'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Plot of probabilities for class Forest produced by LTAE algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/py-fig-ensemble-ltae-probs-1.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: We then compute the variance of the probability cube produced by the LTAE algorithm. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/ensemble-ltae-variance_f80f6e3ee86867456e7c8269c9428e27'} ```{.r .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_variance <- sits_variance( ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_probs, window_size = 9, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "ltae" ) summary(ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_variance) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil Clear_Cut_Burned_Area Clear_Cut_Vegetation Forest 75% 0.840 0.820 1.2800 2.6000 80% 1.340 1.070 1.7300 3.8000 85% 2.340 1.500 2.4100 5.1600 90% 3.721 2.211 3.3500 6.9900 95% 7.110 3.430 4.9205 10.1715 100% 33.640 16.950 30.7500 39.9500 Mountainside_Forest Riparian_Forest Seasonally_Flooded Water Wetland 75% 0.66 2.8500 3.7600 0.4600 1.06 80% 0.83 3.4800 4.6700 0.5500 1.49 85% 1.07 4.3915 5.9415 0.7000 2.28 90% 1.59 5.6900 7.4910 1.0200 3.55 95% 2.77 8.3305 10.9305 9.9635 6.04 100% 10.63 37.9100 44.0500 45.7500 45.64 ``` ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_variance = sits_variance( ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_probs, window_size = 9, output_dir = tempdir_py, multicores = 6, memsize = 24, version = "ltae" ) summary(ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_variance) ``` ::: ::: We use the same rationale for selecting the `smoothness` parameter for the Bayesian smoothing operation as in the cases above. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-ensemble-ltae-class_a3752e0c4c235a44c7f93dcc4173a6d9'} ```{.r .cell-code} ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_bayes <- sits_smooth( ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_probs, output_dir = tempdir_r, window_size = 11, smoothness = c( "Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil" = 1.2, "Clear_Cut_Burned_Area" = 10.0, "Clear_Cut_Vegetation" = 15.0, "Forest" = 4.0, "Mountainside_Forest" = 8.0, "Riparian_Forest" = 25.0, "Seasonally_Flooded" = 30.0, "Water" = 0.3, "Wetland" = 1.8), multicores = 2, memsize = 6, version = "ltae" ) # generate the classified map ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_class <- sits_label_classification( ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_bayes, output_dir = tempdir_r, multicores = 2, memsize = 6, version = "ltae" ) # plot the classified map plot(ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_class, legend_text_size = 0.7, legend_position = "outside") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Classified map produced by LTAE algorithm. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-ensemble-ltae-class-1.png){#fig-ensemble-ltae-class fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Differences between model results To understand the differences between the results, it is useful to compare the resulting class areas produced by the different algorithms, expressed in hectares. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/unnamed-chunk-16_0c4ce9e0bf3ed63b4bad693a42349654'} ```{.r .cell-code} # get the summary of the map produced by RF sum1 <- summary(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_class) |> dplyr::select("class", "area") colnames(sum1) <- c("class", "rfor") # get the summary of the map produced by TCNN sum2 <- summary(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_class) |> dplyr::select("class", "area") colnames(sum2) <- c("class", "tcnn") # get the summary of the map produced by LTAE sum3 <- summary(ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_class) |> dplyr::select("class", "area") colnames(sum3) <- c("class", "ltae") # compare class areas of maps produced by the three models pred_class_areas <- dplyr::inner_join(sum1, sum2, by = "class") |> dplyr::inner_join(sum3, by = "class") pred_class_areas ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 9 × 4 class rfor tcnn ltae 1 Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil 8017. 6818. 6788. 2 Clear_Cut_Burned_Area 185. 280. 282. 3 Clear_Cut_Vegetation 1673. 1204. 1209. 4 Forest 27960. 23696. 23726. 5 Mountainside_Forest 0 0.6 0.12 6 Riparian_Forest 4545. 4055. 3993. 7 Seasonally_Flooded 7581. 13737. 13808. 8 Water 6330. 6624. 6583. 9 Wetland 1309. 1186. 1211. ``` ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd # Get classification summaries sum1 = summary(ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_class) sum2 = summary(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_class) sum3 = summary(ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_class) # Get only ``class`` and ``area`` columns sum1 = sum1[["class", "area"]] sum2 = sum2[["class", "area"]] sum3 = sum3[["class", "area"]] # Rename columns sum1.columns = ["class", "rfor"] sum2.columns = ["class", "tcnn"] sum3.columns = ["class", "ltae"] # Merge columns pred_class_areas = pd.merge(sum1, sum2, on = "class", how = "inner") pred_class_areas = pd.merge(pred_class_areas, sum3, on = "class", how = "inner") pred_class_areas ``` ::: ::: The study area presents many challenges for land classification, given the presence of wetlands, riparian forests and seasonally-flooded areas. The results show the algorithms obtain quite different results, since each model has different sensitivities. The RF method is biased towards the most frequent classes, especially for `Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil` and `Forest`. The area estimated by RF for class `Clear_Cut_Burned_Area` is the smallest of the three models. Most pixels assigned by LTAE and TCNN as burned areas are assigned by RF as being areas of bare soil. The RF algorithm tends to be more conservative. The reason is because RF decision-making uses values from single attributes (values of a single band in a given time instance), while LTAE and TCNN consider the relations between instances of the time series. Since the RF model is sensitive to the response of images at the end of the period, it tends to focus on values that indicate the presence of forests and bare soils during the dry season, which peaks in August. The LTAE and TCNN models are more balanced to the overall separation of classes in the entire attribute space, and produces larger estimates of riparian and seasonally flooded forest than the other methods. In contrast, both LTAE and TCNN make more mistakes than RF in including flooded areas in the center-left part of the image on the left side of the rives as `Clear_Cut_Vegetation` when the right label would be riparian or flooded forests. ## Combining the different predictions Given the differences and complementaries between the three predicted outcomes, combining them using `sits_combine_predictions()` is useful. This function takes the following arguments: (a) `cubes`, a list of the cubes to be combined. These cubes should be probability cubes generated by which optionally may have been smoothened; (b) `type`, which indicates how to combine the probability maps. The options are `average`, which performs a weighted mean of the probabilities, and `uncertainty`, which uses the uncertainty cubes to combine the predictions; (c) `weights`, a vector of weights to be used to combine the predictions when `average` is selected; (d) `uncertainty_cubes`, a list of uncertainty cubes associated to the predictions; (e) `multicores`, number of cores to be used; (f) `memsize`, RAM used in the classification; (g) `output_dir`, the directory where the classified raster files will be written. :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/fig-ensemble-ave-class_6d2147e12eacef3b73bb4f2f7d38b7fc'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Combine the three predictions by taking the average of the probabilities for each class ro_cube_20LMR_average_probs <- sits_combine_predictions( cubes = list(ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_bayes, ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_bayes, ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_bayes), type = "average", version = "average-rfor-tcnn-ltae", output_dir = tempdir_r, weights = c(0.33, 0.34, 0.33), memsize = 16, multicores = 4 ) # Label the average probability cube ro_cube_20LMR_average_class <- sits_label_classification( cube = ro_cube_20LMR_average_probs, output_dir = tempdir_r, version = "average-rfor-tcnn-ltae", memsize = 16, multicores = 4 ) # plot the classified map plot(ro_cube_20LMR_average_class, legend_text_size = 0.7, legend_position = "outside") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Classified map produced by the ensemble of Random Forest, LTAE and TempCNN. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/fig-ensemble-ave-class-1.png){#fig-ensemble-ave-class fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} # Combine the three predictions by taking the average of the probabilities for each class ro_cube_20LMR_average_probs = sits_combine_predictions( cubes = [ ro_cube_20LMR_tcnn_bayes, ro_cube_20LMR_rfor_bayes, ro_cube_20LMR_ltae_bayes ], type = "average", version = "average-rfor-tcnn-ltae", output_dir = tempdir_py, weights = (0.33, 0.34, 0.33), memsize = 16, multicores = 4 ) # Label the average probability cube ro_cube_20LMR_average_class = sits_label_classification( cube = ro_cube_20LMR_average_probs, output_dir = tempdir_py, version = "average-rfor-tcnn-ltae", memsize = 16, multicores = 4 ) # plot the classified map plot(ro_cube_20LMR_average_class, legend_text_size = 0.7, legend_position = "outside") ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" result='false' hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/py-fig-ensemble-ave-class_89dc9cad91be61bf2a7b3385749426db'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Classified map produced by the ensemble of Random Forest, LTAE and TempCNN. ](cl_ensembleprediction_files/figure-html/py-fig-ensemble-ave-class-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: We can also consider the class areas produced by the ensemble combination and compare them to the original estimates, expressed in hectares :::{.panel-tabset} ## R ::: {.cell hash='cl_ensembleprediction_cache/html/unnamed-chunk-19_b2b1f1ff8fa72e46f49e5ccb14bf7d77'} ```{.r .cell-code} # get the summary of the map produced by LTAE sum4 <- summary(ro_cube_20LMR_average_class) |> dplyr::select("class", "area") colnames(sum4) <- c("class", "ave") # compare class areas of non-smoothed and smoothed maps pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae <- dplyr::inner_join(sum1, sum2, by = "class") |> dplyr::inner_join(sum3, by = "class") |> dplyr::inner_join(sum4, by = "class") pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 9 × 5 class rfor tcnn ltae ave 1 Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil 8017. 6818. 6788. 7095. 2 Clear_Cut_Burned_Area 185. 280. 282. 256. 3 Clear_Cut_Vegetation 1673. 1204. 1209. 1134. 4 Forest 27960. 23696. 23726. 24481. 5 Mountainside_Forest 0 0.6 0.12 0.08 6 Riparian_Forest 4545. 4055. 3993. 4201. 7 Seasonally_Flooded 7581. 13737. 13808. 12702. 8 Water 6330. 6624. 6583. 6569. 9 Wetland 1309. 1186. 1211. 1162. ``` ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} # get the summary of the map produced by LTAE sum4 = summary(ro_cube_20LMR_average_class) sum4 = sum4[["class", "area"]] # Rename columns sum4.columns = ["class", "ave"] # compare class areas of non-smoothed and smoothed maps pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae = pd.merge(sum1, sum2, on = "class", how = "inner") pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae = pd.merge(pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae, sum3, on = "class", how = "inner") pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae = pd.merge(pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae, sum4, on = "class", how = "inner") pred_ave_rfor_tcnn_ltae ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 9 × 5 class rfor tcnn ltae ave 1 Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil 8017. 6818. 6788. 7095. 2 Clear_Cut_Burned_Area 185. 280. 282. 256. 3 Clear_Cut_Vegetation 1673. 1204. 1209. 1134. 4 Forest 27960. 23696. 23726. 24481. 5 Mountainside_Forest 0 0.6 0.12 0.08 6 Riparian_Forest 4545. 4055. 3993. 4201. 7 Seasonally_Flooded 7581. 13737. 13808. 12702. 8 Water 6330. 6624. 6583. 6569. 9 Wetland 1309. 1186. 1211. 1162. ``` ::: ::: ::: As expected, the ensemble map combines information from the three models. Taking the RF model prediction as a base, there is a reduction in the areas of classes `Clear_Cut_Bare_Soil` and `Forest`, confirming the tendency of the RF model to overemphasize the most frequent classes. The LTAE and TempCNN models are more sensitive to class variations and capture time-varying classes such as `Riparian_Forest` and `Clear_Cut_Burned_Area` in more detail than the RF model. However, both TempCNN and LTAE tend to confuse the deforestation-related class `Clear_Cut_Vegetation` and the natural class `Riparian_Forest` more than the RF model. This effect is evident in the left bank of the Madeira river in the centre-left region of the image. Also, both the LTAE and TempCNN maps are more grainy and have more spatial variability than the RF map. The average map provides a compromise between RF's strong empahsis on the most frequent classes and the tendency of deep learning methods to produce outliers based on temporal relationship. The average map is less grainy and more spatially consistent than the LTAE and TempCNN maps, while introducing variability which is not present in the RF map. ## Summary This chapter shows the possibilities of ensemble prediction. There are many ways to get better results than those presented here. Increasing the number of spectral bands would improve the final accuracy. Also, Bayesian smoothing for deep learning models should not rely on default parameters; rather it needs to rely on variance analysis, increase the spatial window and provide more informed hyperparameters. In general, ensemble prediction should be consider in all situations where one is not satisfied with the results of individual models. Combining model output increses the reliability of the result and thus should be considered in all situations where similar classes are present.
